newsitem.title: INDIA: Five policemen killed in Indian land mine blast.
newsitem.headline: Five policemen killed in Indian land mine blast.

text.p: Five policemen were killed in a land mine blast set off by left-wing extremists in the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, police said on Sunday.

They said a police team was travelling in a tractor on Saturday evening to Laxmanpur village, about 140 km (88 miles) from the state capital of Hyderabad, to investigate a report that Naxalites had attacked a village when the landmine was detonated by the members of the outlawed People's War Group (PWG).
Five poliemen died on the spot while one managed to escape, officials said. The extremists escaped with arms and ammunition belonging to the police, they said.
Police have launched a search operation in the area.
The PWG is one of many Maoist rebel groups considered part of the Naxalite movement, which started in India in the 1960s among groups which split from the main communist party.
It was first banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 but gained a year-long reprieve beginning in June 1995 before being banned again in July last year.
